relations_to.summary: Stay the security partner of choice for the Pacific through a Pacific-led frame: the Pacific Policing Initiative (endorsed at the Tonga leaders' meeting in August 2024; police centres of excellence, a deployable multi-country force and a Brisbane hub; A$400m over five years in one report) and open backing for the Forum as the region's premier political body (Australia and New Zealand, June 2026); about 120 Pacific police were to deploy to Palau, the largest PPI deployment, for the 55th Leaders' Meeting.

relations_to.summary: Ocean of Peace: Rabuka tabled the idea on 16 Aug 2023; the Pacific Islands Forum leaders endorsed the declaration at the 54th Leaders' Meeting in Honiara in September 2025, rejecting militarisation and great-power rivalry, with Fiji's PM hosting the ceremony. Critics say the Forum sidestepped pressing regional issues.

relations_to.summary: Honiara, as host and chair of the Pacific Islands Forum, kept every dialogue partner out of its 2025 leaders' meeting (the US, China and Taiwan named among the donors left off) and deferred the partner dialogue to 2026; CSIS reads the compromise as shaped by Chinese pressure.

relations_to.summary: At the 54th Leaders' Meeting in Honiara (September 2025) only the Forum's 18 members attended; Prime Minister Manele had told parliament in August that no dialogue partners would be invited. Recorded as expulsion, as TWN.yaml records the same event; the more exact word is exclusion.

relations_to.summary: Tuna access and licence receipts, the largest earner: US$43 million in 2023 (Australian Army country guide), about three-fifths of locally generated government income (APIBC, 2025), down about 40% over five years as stocks move into international waters. The access is sold under the Pacific regime (Nauru Agreement, Forum Fisheries Agency) and the US Tuna Treaty, so the counterparty is the regional arrangement, not one state. Note: no export type fits a fishing-access fee; the value is licence receipts, not trade.

relations_to.summary: At the 2025 Pacific Islands Forum in Honiara the Solomon Islands prime minister, Beijing's closest security partner in the region, announced that the Forum would exclude all partners, China and Taiwan alike; the Taiwan question is described as splintering the Forum. Palau hosted the 2026 meeting, where Taiwan's foreign minister reaffirmed ties.
